statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, r is the maximum size of a non-empty set S of indices with 0 <= i < len(candidates) such that the bitwise AND of the values {candidates[i] | i in S} is greater than 0. Equivalently, both: (1) there is a non-empty index set S with |S| = r and the bitwise AND of {candidates[i] | i in S} > 0; and (2) for every non-empty index set T with 0 <= i < len(candidates) for all i in T, if the bitwise AND of {candidates[i] | i in T} > 0 then |T| <= r. An index set uses each index at most once; its indices need not be contiguous; equal values at different indices are distinct elements.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, go out of bounds, or overflow.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, 1 <= r <= len(candidates).
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, there exists a non-empty set S of indices with 0 <= i < len(candidates) such that |S| = r and the bitwise AND of {candidates[i] | i in S} is greater than 0.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, for every non-empty set S of indices with 0 <= i < len(candidates), if the bitwise AND of {candidates[i] | i in S} is greater than 0, then |S| <= r.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, r = max { c_b | 0 <= b < 63 }, where c_b is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(candidates) whose b-th bit (the bit of weight 2^b) is 1 in candidates[i].
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, r = len(candidates) if and only if the bitwise AND of all elements of candidates is greater than 0.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r and largest_combination(d) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: candidates and d are slices of 64-bit integers, each with 1 <= length <= 100000 and all elements between 1 and 2147483647; d is a permutation of candidates (same length, and for every integer v the number of occurrences of v in d equals the number of occurrences of v in candidates).

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r and largest_combination(d) returns a result r', we have r' <= r.
preconditions: candidates and d are slices of 64-bit integers, each with 1 <= length <= 100000 and all elements between 1 and 2147483647; d is obtained from candidates by deleting zero or more elements (so d is a subsequence of candidates, preserving order).

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if for every pair of distinct indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(candidates), the bitwise AND of candidates[i] and candidates[j] is equal to 0.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, for every bit position b with 0 <= b < 63, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(candidates) whose b-th bit is 1 in candidates[i] is at most r.
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.

statement: Whenever largest_combination(candidates) returns a result r, there exists a bit position b with 0 <= b < 63 such that exactly r indices i with 0 <= i < len(candidates) have the b-th bit set to 1 in candidates[i].
preconditions: candidates is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(candidates) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(candidates), 1 <= candidates[i] <= 2147483647.
